extracted.intended_audience: SABEW members and business journalists (including students, freelancers, and newsroom staff) submitting to the Best in Business Awards
extracted.subtask_description: Submission and eligibility guidelines for entering work in the Society for Advancing Business Editing and Writing (SABEW) Best in Business Awards, including membership, category, format, and fee rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication date eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: This competition covers work published, broadcast and posted in the calendar year 2025. International submissions are encouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Best in Business competition is open to all SABEW members whose membership is current through June 1, 2026. All students can enter, and non-member students will receive a free one-year student membership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For entries with more than one byline, one person must have a current SABEW membership with an expiration date of June 1, 2026, or later. Check membership status/expiration in the membership portal; details on joining or renewing are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership verification at submission
rubrics_metrics.description: When beginning a submission in Award Force, you will be prompted to enter the email address of an active member who is listed as a contributor. The awards program will automatically verify SABEW membership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the contributor is not an active SABEW member, the entry will be ineligible for submission until the membership has been renewed. Entrants are encouraged to check membership status prior to beginning a submission to ensure eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple entries and single-category restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no limit on the number of entries per news outlet; however, any individual story may only be entered into one story type and one story topic category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: the same story or package cannot be entered into both the Investigative and Explanatory categories if those are different story types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Size categories and grouping
rubrics_metrics.description: Categories are broken out by size, determined by the news organization’s total editorial staff: Small: 50 or less editorial staff; Medium: 51-150 editorial staff; Large: 151+ editorial staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: News organizations compete against similarly sized organizations regardless of format. Freelancers will be grouped based on the size of the outlet that published their work. If an entry is the product of a partnership of two or more organizations, enter into the size category corresponding to the combined staffs of the partner organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission platform and overall dates
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions for the 2025 Best in Business Awards are open December 1, 2025, to February 2, 2026. Entries must be submitted through the online platform.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions close on Monday, February 2 at 5 p.m. ET.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadlines and fee tiers
rubrics_metrics.description: There are three deadline tiers (early-bird, competition, late) with different fees tied to each tier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deadlines: Early-bird — Thursday, January 8, 2026 at 5 p.m. ET; Competition — Wednesday, January 28, 2026 at 5 p.m. ET; Late — Monday, February 2, 2026 at 5 p.m. ET. Fees (by deadline): General Excellence categories — $130 / $150 / $200; Story Type, Story Topic categories and Best Range of Work — $79 / $99 / $150; Students — $20 (includes a one-year student membership). Freelance journalists receive a $15 discount per entry using the code 'Freelancer' (not valid for student category entries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry composition: elements limit and types
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise noted, an entry shall consist of no more than three elements. Elements can be text, audio, video, or interactive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elements should all contain the same theme, though they don’t need to be directly related to each other. Accompanying photos and static graphics will not be counted as elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required submission materials (URL, paywall credentials, PDF)
rubrics_metrics.description: Basic requirements include a URL where the entry is live and a username and password if the entry is behind a paywall. A PDF of the entry will also be accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections, retractions, and editors’ notes must be included
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries must include any corrections, retractions, or editors’ notes related to accuracy or fairness that were published in connection to the submitted work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Byline naming and staff entries
rubrics_metrics.description: Up to five individuals may be named on an entry; they should be the strongest contributors to the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries where more than five journalists made substantial contributions must be submitted as a staff entry and individuals will not be named on the award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing entries before final submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries can be saved and edited until the deadline, but corrections cannot be made to entries after submitting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify that all the information in your entry is correct before submitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright and right of use
rubrics_metrics.description: No part of any entry will be returned. SABEW reserves the right to use any part or the whole of any entry for publicity, educational or promotional purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge participation invitation
rubrics_metrics.description: SABEW recruits members to serve as judges for the Best in Business contest and provides a form for interested judges to sign up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judging is presented as an opportunity to read work, meet fellow business journalists, and give back to the profession; members (new and returning) are encouraged to apply.
